title: ay says /ay/
parentNote: A new stage starts today. Until now a vowel said its own name because of a quiet e sitting at the end of the word — cake, bike, home. From today it can say its name because two letters team up and do the job together, and ay is the first of those teams: day, hay, play. The one thing worth telling your child, because it saves a great deal of guessing later on, is that ay lives at the end of a word or the end of a chunk. There is no ay in the middle of anything. The slip to expect is sounding the two letters apart, so day comes out da-yuh. Cover the y, say the a on its own, then uncover it and say the whole word once, as one piece. Say it, don't explain it — the ear gets this one long before the head does.

activities.mouthCue: Your mouth opens wide and then slides shut, and out comes the name of the letter a.
activities.prompt: A new sort of team. These two letters do not say a and y. Together they say the name of the letter a: ay.
Three things an a can be part of. Find the team that says the letter name.
Three vowel teams, three different names. Which one is today's?
Two sounds. Say the d, then the team, and do not let the y speak on its own.
The longest one. Three sounds crowd in at the front and the team is still on the end.
One of these ends with the team and nothing after it. Listen right to the end.
All three start with a p. The next sound, and then the last one, decide it.
Two of these are one sound apart. Listen for an r hiding in the middle.

activities.title: The den in the hay
activities.prompt: Read the story one line at a time. Tap any word you want to hear again.
lines: I want to make a den in the hay.
Bart did say that Fern and I can play in the barn for the day.
Fern and I did stack the hay up and up.
It is a big den, with a hay bed and a hay step.
Then a gray cat came in and did stay.
The cat did not want to play. The cat did nap on the hay bed.
Then the cat did jump up fast. In the hay is a rat!
The rat ran, and the cat ran after it, and the den fell in.
Fern did grin, and I did grin. The cat did not.
It is a big mess, but it is the best day.
